_doc: Spec v1.8 10g.28 (with 10g.7, 10g.17 and the 10g.28 clarifications of 2026-09-28): what a sentence of the current request may carry outside its read; query_selector.unexplained_sentence hands off (unbound_request_constraint) when one of these classes is found. Entries are regex alternatives over canonicalized lower-case text; a list is matched as \b(?:a|b|...)\b. pleasantry and not_ask (a negated ask: 'I don't need tips') are removed before matching. An extra sentence (nothing bound) is checked against every list (high recall: it always handed off before 10g.28). Read wording and small talk, and the sentence that carries the read, are checked only against the lists that cannot be read wording: never *_or_metric, medical_generic (read sentence) or care, which also name metrics, lab groups, profile fields or visits; another person only as a possessive, 'for my X' or the subject of a question; an action only with write_verbs or action_phrases in request form; a clinician only when involved (grammar in query_selector); filter (restrictions on the data selection) never in the read sentence, filter_extra (bare 'only') only in an extra sentence. style (style, format, language) hands off anywhere in the request as text_transformation_requires_native_context. A side sentence whose only binding is a date, next to a sentence that carries the read, is checked like an extra sentence unless it is a plain window clause (its other words are window_words). time_phrases are periods the rule date parser leaves unresolved but the learned parser reads (a part of a day, tonight, a weekday, a weekend, 'N units ago'): a sentence stating one states a date for the sentence roles, like a resolved one. Grammar (request form, clinician involvement, another person, another question) is in query_selector. guards2 additions (spec v1.8 10g.36): unit_phrases and units (unit_conversion: a value asked for in a unit other than the stored one; 'units' maps a catalog unit to its spellings, and a unit that is the native unit of a bound metric is a plain label, not a conversion); medication, medication_change and medication_status (query_selector.medication_change: missed, stopped or changed medication always hands off, next to a plain read too); not_medication (supplements, vitamins and devices are not medication). Round 2 (guards2): prediction (a forecast or a value the user will have: hands off in every role; a modal followed by 'you' is a polite request, not a forecast); supplements and vitamins left the 'care' list (10g.37: plain context) and a supplement phrase is removed before the medical class is matched, so a prescribed or clinician-directed one still hands off through the clinician grammar, '\d+ IU', 'prescribed' and the symptom list. guards38 (spec v1.8 10g.38, same metric in two windows): relative_windows are windows relative to another ('the week before', 'the previous day', '2 weeks earlier', 'the same period last month'); they count as windows for a comparison or a continuation, never as dates for the sentence roles (a sentence with one and anything else, 'What did I eat the day before?', is still an extra sentence: class 8), and they are erased before the date parser reads the rest. One anchored on an event ('the week before my birthday') is not a window (10g.29 analogue), nor is 'the same week' without a shift (the read's own window). window_words also hold interjections ('yo', 'hey'). A side sentence that is only windows and window_words, or a comparison of the read across windows (comparison_window: 'vs last month', 'how does that compare with the week before', 'was it higher than last week', 'put them side by side') when the read and that sentence state two windows none of which is open ('since'; point_in_time counts as the read's window: 'current', 'right now', 'latest'), is a clause-bound continuation (one read per window), not class 5 or 8; against one window the reference is implicit and it stays class 5. A change ('did it improve', 'has it gone up', 'is it up') is such a comparison only before a connector ('from', 'compared to', 'vs') or at the end of the sentence; over a window of its own ('has it improved this month?', 'has it gone up now?') it is a verdict. All current values ('latest', 'right now') are one window. comparison_change (a change or comparative verdict: 'got better', 'whether it dropped', 'I wonder if') hands off in the sentence that carries the read unless that sentence states two windows, no event ('since', 'after', 'before', 'following') and, outside its bound names and windows, nothing but window_words and comparison_frame (the wording of a factual comparative: 'has my', 'got worse', 'than', 'I wonder if'); anything else anywhere in it hands off: a reference ('than usual', 'my baseline', 'Anna's', 'other runners'), a norm ('my ideal weight', 'normal for my age'), a manner ('worryingly'), a reason, purpose or judgement ('... is normal', '... because I'm overtraining'); comparison_read (relationships, causation, norms) always does. style hands off only when the plan is a single read (the direct template; [refined 10g.38]); style_always (unit-system instructions, 10g.36.3, and creative rewrites, which may carry another request: 'write me a haiku about autumn') and translate/rephrase always do. comparison and comparison_read also name a relationship with another series ('on the same track as my step count', 'how closely it tracks').
